pdf_claim: Calef's Battery A, 2nd US (six 3-inch) spent the night of 30 Jun in a hollow; the right and centre sections went about 600 yd forward on the morning of 1 Jul; it fired the first Union gun; Hall's 2nd Maine relieved it about 10:00; improvised field position; the LEFT section was pulled back because the woods came within 200 yd.
corrected_claim: Calef's battery had six 3-inch guns (Hunt). On 30 Jun it went into position 'just outside of town' on what Calef calls the Carlisle road; no source read says 'hollow'. About 8 a.m. on 1 Jul Gamble asked Calef to choose a position; he chose one about 600 yd in front of the night position, a pioneer party levelled the intervening fences and the fence in front of it, and the whole battery moved forward (not only two sections). Buford then had one section placed immediately left of the road (Newman, left section) and one still farther left (Pergel, centre section); Roder's right section fired 'the first gun' on a column of cavalry on the right of the road (Calef's own claim; the NPS handbook repeats it). The section withdrawn because the enemy's woods came within 200 yd of its right was Pergel's CENTRE section, not the left. Hall's 2nd Maine took the first position vacated by Roder's section (NPS: about 10:00; Hunt: ordered in about 10:15; Hall: first fire 10:45); after about half an hour it was disabled and Wadsworth ordered Calef's left and centre sections up again. Calef could serve five guns on 2 Jul. No work of any kind is named: improvised (inferred from a detailed report's silence). The 'First Shot' marker is the Wisler Farm marker for the purported first shot of the battle, not a marker of Calef's gun.

pdf_claim: I Corps batteries under Wainwright (20-22 guns in four batteries) stood on Seminary Ridge behind the E-01 rail barricade from the afternoon of 1 Jul to about 16:30, improvised behind hasty rail works, and withdrew down Chambersburg Street after the line collapsed.
corrected_claim: On the Seminary line Hunt counts sixteen guns concentrated (Cooper's four 3-inch, Stevens' six 12-pdr, Reynolds' L/1st NY six 3-inch) plus Stewart's six 12-pdr = 22 in four batteries; Wainwright counts twelve concentrated (Cooper 4 + Stevens 6 + Wilber's 2) 'hardly 5 yards apart'. The guns did not stand behind the rail barricade: Wainwright put Breck's sections behind 'a strong stone wall on the seminary crest', Cooper stood in front of the professor's house, Stevens on Cooper's right, Stewart half between the Cashtown pike and the railroad and half across the railroad in the corner of a wood; the loose-rail breastwork was an infantry work some 40 yd down the slope in front of a battery (Robinson). There is no gun pit or earth. Clocks: batteries came into the seminary position between about noon and a few minutes past 2 p.m.; the retreat began when the infantry fell back (Hunt: about 4 p.m. for the troops; Cooper: about 5 p.m. when the battery retired through Gettysburg). They moved off down the Cashtown pike at a walk, then a trot, through the town (the OR does not name Chambersburg Street) to Cemetery Hill; Wilber's last gun was lost. Losses 83 men and about 80 horses (Hunt, Wainwright).

corrected_claim: Johnson's report names Andrews' battalion (Major J. W. Latimer commanding) as Raine's, Dement's, Brown's and Carpenter's batteries; Graham's battery (1st Virginia Artillery, Rockbridge) 'aided'. Andrews' own report counts fourteen guns of the battalion on the hill plus two 20-pounder Parrotts placed on an eminence in rear 'with Captain Graham's battery'; the New York book of 1900 counts twenty guns in all (14 + six 20-pounder Parrotts of Graham's and Raine's batteries), which is the PDF's 'about 20'. The hill is the 'only eligible' one, a little left of Cemetery Hill and in front of the wooded mountain (Culp's Hill), exposed to concentrated fire from both and an enfilade from a battery near the Baltimore road; Andrews found great difficulty sheltering horses and caissons; no works are named. Opening: 4 p.m. (Johnson, Brown, Pendleton, Andrews), about 5 p.m. (Ewell); the Union side puts the Confederate battery in action about 3:30 (Hunt) or about 4 p.m. (Wainwright) and counts ten guns. The fight lasted about two hours (Johnson, Cooper 2.5 h, Wainwright 1.5 h, Ewell one hour). Latimer withdrew all but four guns (Johnson, Andrews) = one battery (Brown, Ewell) and was mortally wounded with them. The name 'Benner's Hill' is not in the OR; Bachelder (1873, 1889), Maine at Gettysburg and New York at Gettysburg use it. The 37-gun Union figure is in no source read. Union witnesses: four limbers or caissons exploded; two guns drawn off by hand; 28 dead horses on the knoll.
